correctness.rationale: The threshold reconstruction is sound. For an upward-flat relation on the chain, each row is a suffix and hence has a unique threshold \(t_i\). Direct composition shows reflexivity of \(\leq\circ R\) is equivalent to the suffix minimum \(m_i=\min_{u\ge i}t_u\) satisfying \(m_i\le i\); transitivity is equivalent to every finite threshold value \(q\) satisfying \(m_q=q\). These conditions make \(m\) a nondecreasing regressive idempotent. Its fixed-point plateaux give exactly the stated product count, and summing over fixed sets gives \(B_{n+1}-B_n\). I independently exhaustively replayed every threshold vector through \(n=6\), obtaining \(1,3,10,37,151,674\), with the next Bell difference \(3263\). The finite replay checks the reduction, while the all-\(n\) conclusion rests on the proved plateau bijection and Bell identity.
residual_risks: The theorem is for the fixed finite chain with the stated composition convention; it does not enumerate arbitrary finite posets.
